Options + answer: a thin stripMasked kernel, only these rows

Rows: the word doing the reading. Columns: the words it can see. Q = question, A and B = two options, Ans = answer token.

Making it fast

Prism started at 664 ms per median request, running in 16-bit precision across two B200 GPUs. We converted the weights to FP8 so the model fits on a single GPU, ran all 128 experts in one grouped kernel, captured the forward pass as a CUDA Graph, folded the FP8 conversion into the expert kernels, and merged the fine-tuning adapter into the model weights. Together, these bring the median request to 44 ms, 15× faster than where we started, with no drop in accuracy.

Using Prism

Prism’s weights are on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence. Prism runs in FP8 on one GPU with at least 120 GB of memory. It is also available on the Sarvam API at Sarvam Indus. India unveiled three indigenous artificial intelligence foundation models yesterday as part of the government's IndiaAI Mission, marking a significant step in building domestic AI capabilities.

The models—Soket's EKA-1 and ZenteiQ's Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B—were unveiled at an event in New Delhi in the presence of IT secretary S Krishnan.

Both startups were selected under the mission's IndiaAI Innovation Centre pillar to develop domestic foundation models.

Soket's 26.3 billion parameter EKA-1 model has been trained on nearly 7.5 trillion tokens and supports all 22 scheduled Indian languages as well as English.

EKA-1 targets mathematics, coding, reasoning and agentic use cases, while Dhīr models focus on smaller multilingual assistants that can operate in environments with limited connectivity.
